# Final-evaluation results (generated by experiments/make_results_md.py)

All numbers below are produced by `./run_final.sh`; figures are in `experiments/figures/`.
Platform unless stated: 1x H100-class GPU, 80 GB HBM3 (3.35 TB/s), Mixtral-8x7B FP16, all
experts in off-chip CPU DRAM behind a 900 GB/s NVLink-C2C link (SSD-offloading `offload_bandwidth: 5`).
Expert = 352.3 MB, load 391.5 us, execution of 1 token ~144 us (HBM bandwidth minus link bandwidth).

## V. Validation

* 144 simulated batches (288 simulator runs, compute + copy mode); routing executed by the simulator == routing trace: **True**.
* Timeline cost model vs simulator `expert_ffn` (compute and copy mode), worst relative error **3.0e-14**; offload bytes vs `moe_offload` energy: 7.0e-08 (float32 energy constants).
* Midterm D2 configs re-run on the modified simulator: load 68.13 ms, exec 25.02 ms, max relative difference to the committed midterm CSVs 5.4e-08.

## F2-F4. Prefetching vs on-demand execution

Latency per decode step (= per generated token of each sequence), expert-load time (link busy
copying experts), exposed expert-load stall (GPU idle waiting for a copy),
DRAM->HBM traffic, energy per generated token.  Speed-up / savings relative to on-demand + LRU
at the same cache capacity.  Mean over independent sequence groups (H100: B=1 16, B=4 8, B=8 4 groups;
B=4/8 use all 32 evaluation sequences; A100 and the ablation: 8 groups at B=1), with the min-max
speed-up over groups in brackets.
